lines.cap: He screwed one buyer so well, that he came back to do it again.
lines.say: He screwed one buyer so well, that he came back to do it again.

lines.cap: Victor Lustig. A con man, in Paris, in 1925.
lines.say: Victor Lustig. A con man, in Paris, in 1925.

lines.cap: He read that the Eiffel Tower was rusting, and costly to repair. So he had an idea.
lines.say: He read that the Eiffel Tower was rusting, and costly to repair. So he had an idea.

lines.cap: He posed as a government official, and invited scrap metal dealers to a secret meeting, in a fancy hotel.
lines.say: He posed as a government official, and invited scrap metal dealers to a secret meeting, in a fancy hotel.

lines.cap: The Eiffel Tower is being torn down, he said. Who wants the metal? A dealer named André Poisson paid him, plus a bribe.
lines.say: The Eiffel Tower is being torn down, he said. Who wants the metal? A dealer named André Poisson paid him, plus a bribe.

lines.cap: Lustig fled with the cash. Poisson was too embarrassed to tell the police.
lines.say: Lustig fled with the cash. Poisson was too embarrassed to tell the police.

lines.cap: So Lustig came back, and tried the same trick on new dealers. This time, one went to the police. He escaped to America.
lines.say: So Lustig came back, and tried the same trick on new dealers. This time, one went to the police. He escaped to America.

lines.cap: He sold a tower he never owned.
lines.say: He sold a tower he never owned.
